sections.title: Power details mechanics
lines: Poison Lash · Melee basic attack, reach 2 squares. Poison keyword.
Foot Snare · Reach 4 squares. A hit knocks the target prone.
Lashing Vines · Healing keyword. Close burst 4 against enemies. Each hit on an immobilized target deals an extra 1d8 damage and restores 5 HP to the vine.
Rapid Growth · Encounter power. When first bloodied, the vine spawns two Ambush Vine Shoots within 4 squares. They act immediately after the vine on its initiative count.
Sprout Vine · At-will minor action. The vine takes 10 damage and spawns one Ambush Vine Shoot within 4 squares. The shoot acts immediately after the vine on its initiative count.

sections.title: Ambush Vine Shoot mechanics
lines: Level 15 Minion Controller · Medium fey beast (plant), 300 XP. Initiative +14, Perception +14, tremorsense 20, AC 29, Fortitude 27, Reflex 30, Will 23. Speed 6 squares and burrow 6. It has 1 HP and takes no damage from a missed attack.
Wrapping Vines · Standard at-will melee basic attack, reach 2 squares. +20 vs. Fortitude. Hit for 12 damage and restrain the target (save ends).
Enwrap · Enemies adjacent to the shoot take a −2 penalty to saving throws against immobilized and restrained.
Ability scores and Stealth · Str 18, Dex 25, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 15, Cha 12. Stealth +19, or +24 in undergrowth, trees, or swamps. Unaligned. No languages.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: August 2012 update, p. 82, corrects the parent vine’s original 1,400 XP to 2,800 XP. The shoot’s 300 XP comes from its own block.
Unaligned. No languages. Saving throws +2 and one action point. Stealth rises from +20 to +25 in undergrowth, trees or swamp.
The vine stalks prey through canopy, soil and water. It can hide underground or blend with surrounding plants.
Source: Wizards of the Coast, Monster Manual 2 (4e), pp. 204–205, with the August 2012 Rules Update, p. 82.

sections.title: Power details mechanics
lines: Bite · Melee basic attack.
Sting · Melee basic attack with the Poison keyword.
Flyby Attack · At-will standard action. Fly up to 8 squares and make one melee basic attack along that route. Moving away from that target does not provoke its opportunity attacks.
Invisibility · Standard action with the Illusion keyword. It recharges when the pseudodragon takes damage. Invisibility lasts while the pseudodragon stays still.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: August 2012 update, p. 77, changes the original size from Tiny to Small. The checked Deluxe page already shows Small.
Unaligned. No languages. It communicates with animal noises. Wild pseudodragons hunt other creatures and usually leave humanoids alone unless provoked. Some live with humanoids as pets.
The tactics use Sting during a Flyby Attack when it is available. Against a persistent enemy the pseudodragon shifts, then uses Invisibility.
Source: Wizards of the Coast, Monster Manual (4e Deluxe), pp. 90–92, with the August 2012 Rules Update, p. 77.

sections.title: Traits
lines: Keen Senses. The pseudodragon has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, hearing, or smell. Magic Resistance. The pseudodragon has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Limited Telepathy. The pseudodragon can magically communicate simple ideas, emotions, and images telepathically with any creature within 100 feet of it that can understand a language.

lines: Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage. Sting. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 hour. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target falls unconscious for the same duration, or until it takes damage or another creature uses an action to shake it awake.
